extracted.intended_audience: investigators preparing the Vertebrate Animals section of an NIH grant (IACUC/institutional compliance officers and grant reviewers)
extracted.subtask_short: vertebrate animals section for NIH grant
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and required content for the Vertebrate Animals portion of an NIH grant/progress report describing use of mice in biomedical research, including justification, numbers, husbandry, veterinary care, pain/distress minimization, and euthanasia.

rubrics_metrics.name: IACUC approval and institutional compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The mice used in this proposal will be from protocols approved by the Mayo Clinic Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC). Mayo Clinic assures strict compliance with all federal regulations and guidelines involving the use of laboratory animals in biomedical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All protocols presently being conducted and those proposed, regardless of funding sources, are reviewed and must be approved before their initiation. Animal use assurances have been filed with the IACUC and the NIH. The institution monitors adherence to these procedures. Protocols are active for 3 years after the approval date. Facility accreditation (AAALAC) and institutional registrations/assurances (USDA registration, NIH OLAW assurance A3291-01) should be stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed description of animal use (species, strains, ages, sex, numbers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a detailed description of the use of animals in the research. Identify species, strains, ages, sex, and numbers of animals to be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List the exact mouse lines to be used and give per-protocol breakdowns (examples provided: FOXP3ΔEZH2; B6129S-Tg(Foxp3-EGFP/cre)1aJbs/J; Foxp3tm9(EGFP/cre/ERT2)Ayr/J; FOXP3ΔIL6R; C57/BL6CAR; C57BL/6-Foxp3tm1Flv/J; B6.129S7-Rag1tm1Mom/J; C57/BL6 EZH2flox/flox). Provide anticipated numbers per experiment and per year; give totals by strain and across the project period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification of the use and number of animals and choice of species
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify the use and number of animals and choice of species with additional justification if animals are in short supply or are costly or if you plan to use large numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why alternatives are not available (e.g., no safe human or in vitro options) and why the chosen species/models are required to answer the scientific question. Provide experimental reasoning for numbers (see statistical/power justification) and describe plans to limit animal numbers. Example: mice are required because epigenetic questions in intestinal Treg development cannot be answered in vitro; breeding requirements justify numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search for alternatives and avoidance of unnecessary duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe searches, sources, or methods used to determine that alternatives to procedures causing pain/distress are not available and that the protocol does not unnecessarily duplicate previous experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List databases searched and keywords used (examples: Medline, Current Research Information Services (CRIS), Animal Welfare Information Center (AWIC), PUBMED; keywords: animal model; colitis; FOXP3; IL6; EZH2; years searched: 1980–2014). Document search strategy so reviewers can assess whether alternatives were adequately considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical justification / power analysis for group sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the statistical basis for group sizes (power analysis) and number of animals per group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided: one-way ANOVA analysis to allow 90% power when differences between colitis are 1.25 standard deviations more than controls; therefore 4 recipient mice per treatment group were used in calculations. Show calculations and how replication/triplicates affect total animal numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide per-protocol animal number calculations and replication rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Break down animal requirements by experimental protocol and show how experimental design (replicates, number of constructs, triplicates) drives animal counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: in vitro suppression assays require approximately 3 spleens per assay; for 3 constructs in triplicate anticipate 27 FOXP3ΔEZH2 mice and 9 WT mice; in vivo colitis rescue uses 4 RAGnull recipients per treatment, repeated 3 times, etc. Use these calculations to justify totals and to plan donor vs recipient needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total animal numbers and multi-year totals by strain
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide total anticipated animal requirements across study duration, including breeding animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example totals provided: WT=150/yr (750 over 5yr) + breeding; IL6mt=100/yr (500 over 5yr) + breeding; FOXP3ΔEZH2=100/yr (500 over 5yr) + breeding; RAGnull=84 total; TOTAL = 2139 mice over 5 years (428 per year). Include breeding and recipient/donor breakdowns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breeding justification and maintenance plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe breeding strategies and justify breeder numbers needed to maintain required genotypes and supply experimental animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide genotype frequencies and breeding ratios (example: CRE+, heterozygous EZH2WT/flox bred to EZH2flox/flox yields ~20% desired genotype). State breeder-to-experimental-animal ratios (example: for every 6 animals used, typically 1 breeder pair required). Explain any intensive breeding needs (e.g., tamoxifen-inducible lines) and include breeder counts in totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Veterinary care and housing facility description
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide information on veterinary care for the animals and describe housing conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State that animals are housed in a pathogen-free laminar flow facility with controlled temperature, humidity and lighting; food/water provision and cage cleaning frequency; name veterinary oversight (example: three full-time veterinarians certified in laboratory animal medicine and veterinary pathology). State facility accreditation and institutional registrations (AAALAC-accredited, USDA registration, NIH assurance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures to limit discomfort, pain, and distress; analgesics/anesthetics and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe procedures for ensuring that discomfort, pain, and injury will be limited to what is unavoidable, including use of analgesic, anesthetic, tranquilizing drugs, and restraining devices to minimize distress, pain, and injury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State that investigators must administer appropriate analgesics for procedures that would normally require pain medication in humans. Provide monitoring plans (example: animals weighed and examined daily while in study). Define stopping rules (example: experiments ended at predefined time points OR when animals have lost more than 20% of starting body weight or exhibit a moribund appearance). Describe routine care (clean, climate-controlled environment; controlled light-dark cycle; feed/water daily; cages cleaned weekly). Include procedure-specific care (example: Tylenol overnight following adoptive transfer; brief restraint in plexiglass cylinder for tail vein injection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Humane endpoints and criteria for euthanasia
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe humane endpoints, reasons for euthanasia, and who may authorize euthanasia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State that requests to perform euthanasia are reviewed and approved by IACUC; euthanasia may be performed to terminate a study, relieve pain/distress unalleviated by analgesics, or if deemed necessary by the consulting veterinarian. Define clinical criteria and monitoring frequency that trigger euthanasia (example: >20% weight loss, moribund appearance, excessive stress/pain/discomfort).

rubrics_metrics.name: Euthanasia methods and compliance with AVMA guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any euthanasia method to be used and the reasons for its selection. State whether this method is consistent with AVMA Guidelines on Euthanasia and justify deviations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: CO2 inhalation used with listed justifications (rapid depressant/analgesic/anesthetic effects; availability; low hazard). Explicitly state consistency with AVMA Panel on Euthanasia or provide justification if not consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex inclusion and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: State which sexes will be used and provide justification for use of both sexes or a single sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: experiments performed on both male and female WT mice with similar results; therefore plan to use both. If single-sex studies are proposed, justify why the other sex is excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and protocol review frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe recordkeeping and the timeframe that protocols remain active after approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: protocols are reviewed and approved by IACUC before initiation and remain active for 3 years after approval. Ensure documentation of approvals, assurances filed with IACUC/NIH, and oversight procedures are described.
